title: Odd-Parity Crystalline Electric Field and Multipoles in Icosahedral Quasicrystal and Approximant: Magnetic Toroidal and Electric Dipoles in Ce-Based Systems
authors: Shinji Watanabe, Syunta Furuya, Mitsuaki Kawamura
abstract: Quasicrystals (QCs) lack periodic arrangement of atoms but possess unique structural order distinct from periodic crystals and random systems. The electronic property is far from complete understanding. Here we have formulated not only even-parity but also odd-parity crystalline electric field (CEF) in the Ce-based icosahedral QC and approximant crystal (AC) on the basis of the point charge model. Under the odd-parity CEF due to local-inversion symmetry breaking at the Ce site, the hybrid wavefunction of 4f and 5d states at Ce is shown to give rise to the odd-parity multipoles such as electric dipole and magnetic toroidal (MT) dipole. We have found that the vortex order in the 1/1 AC where the magnetic moments on each icosahedron swirl is characterized by the cluster-type MT moment. The ferroic alignment of the cluster MT moments in the vortex order gives rise to the electro-magnetic effect. The cluster-MT moment is shown to be resonated with the MT dipole moments in each icosahedron by tuning the 4f energy level and 5d energy level so as to approach. We have revealed a noncollinear magnetic structure is stabilized in the ground state of the icosahedral QC cluster, behind which there exists underlying mechanism to prefer the ferroic interaction for the net MT dipole moments between the icosahedrons. We point out that the 4f and 5d energy levels can be made approach at the valence transition or the valence crossover, which is ubiquitous in the rare-earth based ACs and QCs.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the electronic structure of Ce-based icosahedral quasicrystals by formulating an odd-parity Crystalline Electric Field theory. This theory predicts the existence of odd-parity multipoles, such as the magnetic toroidal dipole, which are crucial for understanding the material's exotic magnetic and electronic behavior. The findings suggest underlying mechanisms favoring ferroic interactions in these complex, non-periodic materials.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the electronic properties, particularly the crystalline electric field (CEF) and associated multipoles, in Icosahedral Quasicrystals (QCs) and their approximant crystals (ACs).
main_result: The odd-parity CEF, arising from local inversion symmetry breaking, leads to odd-parity multipoles like electric and magnetic toroidal dipoles, stabilizing noncollinear magnetic structures.
method: The research employs theoretical formulation based on the point charge model to derive the CEF Hamiltonian, followed by calculating expectation values for multipole operators.
model_or_system: The system under study is Ce-based icosahedral QCs and ACs. The theoretical framework involves deriving both even- and odd-parity CEF Hamiltonians for the $4f$ electrons.
key_observables: Odd-parity multipoles (electric dipole, magnetic toroidal dipole), cluster-type MT moment, and the magnetic easy axis direction.
important_parameters: The $4f$ and $5d$ energy levels, and the valence ratio ($\alpha$) in the approximant crystal.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the local coordination environment and utilizes the point charge model for the CEF calculation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the atomic structure of the 1/1 AC, the local Ce coordination environment, and phase diagrams showing magnetic ground states based on varying parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the structural context of QCs, formulating the necessary odd-parity CEF theory due to symmetry breaking, and culminating in the calculation of specific odd-parity multipole expectation values.
why_interesting: The focus on symmetry breaking (odd-parity terms) and the emergence of exotic multipoles like the magnetic toroidal dipole connects to advanced topics in condensed matter magnetism and electronic structure.
